findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: None of the employees are food manager certified. Discussed with the owner the need to have at least two employees manager certified to be sure that all hours of operation are covered. A reference sheet for CFM courses was given to the person in charge. Ensure that there is always a person on site who is food manager certified if serving food.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: There were no completed employee health forms on site for food employees. Blank employee health forms were given to the PIC to have all employees complete. Ensure that signed forms are available for all employees and keep on file for future routine inspections. Will follow-up on December 1, 2026 to see that forms have been signed by all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There weren’t any paper towels available at the kitchen handwashing sink. Discussed with the PIC and paper towels were provided to the hand-sink to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are stocked with paper towel.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The facility was unaware of the required sanitizing procedures and proper chemical usage for food contact surfaces. There is a dish machine within the kitchen space, however, the machine isn't functioning properly and there isn't a plan to use the machine for sanitizing dishes, according to the owner. Discussed with the PIC the proper way to wash, rinse, and sanitize dishes in triple sink as an alternative. The PIC indicated that the facility will use chlorine to sanitize dishes in the future. A sanitizer solution was created to sanitize dishes for the mean time using quaternary ammonia. Will follow-up on December 1, 2026 to ensure that bleach has been purchased and will be available for use.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were various time/temperature control (TCS) foods that lacked proper date marking and were unlabeled inside of the main cooler. Discussed with the PIC the need to date mark and label TCS foods that will be stored in house longer than 24 hours. Ensure that TCS foods are marked with the preparation or discard date (and label to identify item). Will follow-up on December 1, 2026 to see that foods have been date marked and labeled.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed fish thawing in a plastic container under standing water. Discussed with PIC that TCS foods that are thawing must be thawed using an approved method. Either place items under cool running water with a constant flow, under refrigeration, or during the cooking process. Ensure to using either method when thawing TCS foods. Will follow-up on December 1, 2026 to ensure that improper thawing methods have been ceased.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There aren’t any probe thermometers available on site to accurately measure food temperatures. Discussed with the PIC the importance of having probe thermometers on site. Ensure that probe style thermometers are purchased and are being used to verify cooking temperatures for foods being served. Will follow-up on December 1, 2026 to see that probe thermometers have been purchased and are available for use.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There aren't any test strips available to test chemical sanitizer. The proper test strips were shown to the PIC. Inspector also demonstrated how to accurately measure the chemical’s concentration. Will follow up December 1, 2026 to see that test strips have been purchased.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
None of the employees are food handler certificated. Discussed with the owner that all employees handling food or either clean dishes will need to at least obtain a food handler certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.
